newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu backs additional 1997 budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu backs additional 1997 budget cuts.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday the government had to cut a total of six billion to seven billion shekels from the 1997 budget.

"If we do not cut six to seven billion (shekels) there will be a collapse," a spokeswoman for Netanyahu's Likud party quoted Netanyahu telling a closed meeting of the Likud faction in parliament. The spokeswoman gave no further details.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor said earlier on Tuesday he would seek a further two billion shekels in budget cuts for 1997 on top of the 4.9 billion shekels already proposed.
"We estimate that we are short on the income side for 1997 an amount that could reach two billion shekels," Meridor said.

The minister would not say when he would ask parliament to approve the additional cuts nor would he say where he would make them. A senior government official said on Monday that additional cuts would not be made to the defence budget.

Meridor already faces considerable opposition in parliament to the 4.9 billion shekel cut, even among coalition members. Parliament is now debating the 190.8 billion shekel budget and has until December 31 to approve it.
Opponents say the reductions will hit lower-income groups hardest. Meridor warned that parliament's failure to approve the spending cuts would have severe effects on the economy.
